official.deadline_note: Boren Fellowships deadline is 20 January 2027 at 5pm Eastern; Boren Scholarships deadline is 27 January 2027 at 5pm Eastern. Campus representatives may set earlier campus deadlines that must also be respected. 2027-28 funding may be applied to programs starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028.
official.application_cycle: 2027-28 cycle; applications open, funding may be applied to programs starting as early as June 2027 or as late as March 1, 2028
official.status_note: The Apply Now page states the 2027-2028 Boren Scholarship and Boren Fellowship application cycles are open.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Eligible expenses include 'Approved program tuition and fees' and 'Home institution matriculation fees, up to $2,500/semester ($5,000 overall cap)'.
official.funding_period: maximum award determined by duration abroad
benefits: $8,000 for 8-11 weeks, a summer program for STEM majors only (Boren Scholarships)
Regional Flagship Language Initiative: approved summer domestic cost PLUS $12,500 for 12-24 weeks overseas or $25,000 for 25-52 weeks overseas
eligibility: U.S. citizens at the time of the national application deadline; no permanent residents or international students are eligible
At least 18 years of age by the time the application is submitted, and a high school graduate or GED holder

Matriculated for the duration of the funded program in an undergraduate (Boren Scholarships) or graduate (Boren Fellowships) degree program in the United States accredited by a body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
Planning an overseas program outside Western Europe, Canada, Australia, or New Zealand, in a destination of which the applicant is not a citizen
ROTC cadets, midshipmen and members of the military Reserves or National Guard must be in inactive, non-drilling status for the duration of the funded program

Preference is given to preferred-duration programs, intensive study of a preferred language in a preferred overseas destination, preferred fields of study, and longer-term interest in a federal career
requirements: Commit to working in the federal government in support of U.S. national security for at least one year after graduation
All Boren Awards-funded programs must include language study within a classroom as a core element for the duration of the grant, with at least 15-20 weekly language hours
Grantees must remain matriculated in a U.S. degree program for the duration of the funded program and may not graduate until it is complete
Financial aid from other sources applied to the overseas program must be reported and may affect the total Boren Awards grant; student loans will not affect the grant
Travel supported by the award must comply with the Fly America Act, with passenger receipt pages submitted to show compliance
documents: Unofficial transcripts from the current institution (and any institution where credit was received), redacted of sensitive personal identifying information
Two letters of recommendation (a third may be included), submitted by the recommenders themselves
A Language Evaluation of the Boren language, encouraged from a recent instructor in that language
A study abroad program description upload, limited to no more than 5 pages
Alternate study abroad program details where required (asterisked destinations and Arabic, Mandarin or Russian)
selection_criteria: A clear and compelling explanation of the significance of the overseas destination, region, language, field of study, and study to U.S. national security, drawing on the applicant's academic perspectives and goals for national security employment (Tier One priority organizations: the Departments of War, State, and Homeland Security, and the Intelligence Community)
Demonstrated understanding of how the federal service requirement will be fulfilled and a longer-term commitment to federal government service
A serious commitment to language study before, during and after the overseas program, with realistic proficiency goals and the minimum 15-20 weekly contact hours
A study plan in a preferred overseas destination and preferred language, a preferred field of study, and the preferred duration of 25+ weeks
Appropriate academic preparation, adaptability, flexibility and maturity to succeed abroad
Veterans of the U.S. armed forces receive selection preference when other factors are equivalent
coverage: Home institution matriculation fees, up to $2,500/semester ($5,000 overall cap)
Fly America Act compliant round-trip airfare at the lowest cost unrestricted class, checked luggage (up to 2 bags), overseas health insurance, local transportation, and cybersecurity costs up to $500
application_method: Visit the Apply Now page and create a new application at apply.iie.org (separate applications for Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships), selecting the overseas location and language to be studied
Reach out to the Boren Awards campus representative at your institution as early as possible and respect any campus deadline set (applicants without a representative may still apply)
Watch the introductory webinar and review the official selection criteria

Complete the twelve application sections: eligibility determination, personal and academic information, employment history, activities, program information and budget, essays, language self-assessment, additional information, recommendations, submission agreement, and review
Send essays to recommenders early and use 'Add Recommender' to notify two recommenders (a third is optional) and any language evaluator
Submit by the national deadline at 5pm Eastern, using the Review section to correct flagged errors before clicking 'Submit Application'
official.application_route: Create the online application at apply.iie.org via the Boren Awards Apply Now page (separate Scholarship and Fellowship applications).
official.citizenship_residency: U.S. citizens only at the time of the national application deadline; permanent residents and international students are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: Not open to international students or permanent residents; U.S. citizenship is required.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Classroom language study must be the core element of the funded program (at least 15-20 weekly language hours). Preference is given to preferred languages, preferred overseas destinations (Africa, Asia, Central & Eastern Europe, Latin America, and the Middle East) and preferred fields of study including STEM, area studies, languages, international affairs, political science and others; applicants from other fields must explain how they will be competitive for specific public service careers.
official.research_requirement: Boren Fellows may conduct research related to theses or dissertations abroad alongside language study, and applicants proposing internships, other classroom study or research are strongly advised to secure letters of affiliation from overseas host institutions or faculty and attach them to their applications.
official.duration: Minimum 12 weeks for most applicants; a special exception allows undergraduate STEM majors to propose summer programs of 8 weeks or longer; preference is given to programs of at least 25 weeks, and programs of two or more semesters are strongly encouraged.
official.description: The National Security Education Program (NSEP) awards Boren Scholarships to U.S. undergraduate students and Boren Fellowships to U.S. graduate students committed to long-term overseas study in world regions critical to U.S. interests and to federal service. Boren Awards funding is designed to cover the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses but is not all-inclusive.
official.region: Preferred overseas destinations in Africa, Asia, Central & Eastern Europe, Latin America, and the Middle East; Western Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand are always ineligible.
official.program_type: Federal overseas study and research awards (Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships) under the National Security Education Program, an initiative of the Defense Language and National Security Education Office (DLNSEO)

not_confirmed: english_requirement - the official pages publish no English proficiency requirement; the only published proficiency rule concerns French and Spanish (intermediate high, ILR 1+ or greater in Speaking, for advanced study programs in Africa and Latin America)
study_mode - the official pages do not label the funded programs as full-time or part-time
Number of awards offered per cycle is not published
verification.notes: Award tiers ($8,000/$12,500/$25,000), eligible and ineligible cost categories, 2027 national deadlines, selection criteria, application sections and the open 2027-28 cycle were verified on the awarding body's own pages at borenawards.org on 2026-10-10.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a U.S.-citizens-only award that pays up to $25,000 for 25-52 weeks of classroom-based language study in a preferred overseas destination, in exchange for at least one year of federal service after graduation. The 2027-28 cycle is open with a 20 January 2027 deadline for Fellowships and 27 January 2027 for Scholarships, both at 5pm Eastern, and funding can be applied to programs starting between June 2027 and 1 March 2028. Eligible costs run from tuition and matriculation fees to housing, food, insurance, visas and Fly America-compliant airfare, but the award is capped by duration and is explicitly not all-inclusive, so budget a personal contribution. Preference is strongly on the side of longer programs (25+ weeks) in preferred languages and destinations.
applicant_utility.best_fit: U.S. undergraduates and graduate students who can genuinely commit to a federal career and want deep, long-duration language immersion outside Western Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact your Boren Awards campus representative as early as possible and ask whether they set an internal campus deadline
Verify your proposed program delivers at least 15-20 weekly contact hours of formal language acquisition

Check your destination on the preferred-destination map: asterisked (blue) destinations are unlikely to be approved for 2027 travel and require a viable alternate program, as do Arabic, Mandarin and Russian applicants (except Mandarin in Taiwan and Arabic in Morocco)
Redact any SSN or date of birth from your unofficial transcripts before uploading
Register two recommenders in the system and share essay drafts with them early, and line up a recent language instructor for the optional Language Evaluation
Submit well before 5pm Eastern on your national deadline and clear every flagged error in the Review section
common_rejection_risks: Proposing an asterisked destination or Arabic/Mandarin/Russian without a viable alternate in an unrestricted destination for the same language
Proposing under 25 weeks without a compelling case, since preference goes to longer programs and the funding tier is set by duration

Essays that fail to tie the destination, language, field of study and career plan to U.S. national security and federal service, or that touch the prohibited topics of gender ideology, diversity equity and inclusion, and environmental justice
A program where English-taught coursework dominates or weekly language contact hours fall below the 15-20 minimum
Respecting the national deadline but missing an earlier campus representative deadline
Studying French or Spanish without the tested proficiency level the award will be contingent upon
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Passport fees, medical expenses including vaccinations, copays, treatment and COVID testing, a personal laptop, dependent expenses, personal travel or entertainment, U.S.-side domestic costs such as rent, car or student-loan payments, and anything above the duration-tier maximum.
document_audit: Transcripts must be unofficial yet show your name, institution, course titles and grades; any social security number or date of birth must be redacted before upload
Recommenders submit their own letters and language evaluations - you cannot upload on their behalf and will only see submission status
Letters from a parent, sibling or other relative are not accepted
The study abroad program description upload is capped at 5 pages
An alternate program in the same language but an unrestricted destination is mandatory for asterisked destinations and Arabic, Mandarin and Russian applicants
alerts: Duration tiers are firm: 24 weeks and a few days does not round up to the 25-week $25,000 tier
Any award granted for the study of French or Spanish is contingent upon verification through testing of the student's language level
Other scholarships or aid must be reported and will reduce the Boren award if they cover the same costs (e.g. tuition or airfare)
Funding for program expenses incurred after May 31, 2028 is contingent upon availability and cannot be guaranteed at the time of award
You may adjust your proposed program after applying only within the same language, same destination and similar weekly language intensity
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Build the application at apply.iie.org via the Apply Now page, complete all twelve sections, have recommenders submit directly, clear the Review-section errors, and click 'Submit Application' before 5pm Eastern on the national deadline.

official.deadline_note: Spring 2027 admission through AUWCL and scholarship application: residential LL.M. 1 November 2026; hybrid and online LL.M. 30 November 2026. Fall 2026 deadlines were 1 May 2026 (residential) and 1 June 2026 (hybrid/online).
official.status_note: The OAS Scholarships page lists the OAS - AUWCL announcement under 2026 open announcements with Spring 2027 admission and scholarship application deadlines of 1 November 2026 (onsite) and 30 November 2026 (hybrid/online).
official.tuition_coverage_note: Benefits: '50% Tuition waiver'. The published total tuition of USD 61,944 leaves USD 30,972 to be covered by the scholar, i.e. the waiver covers 50% of tuition.
official.funding_period: per LL.M. programme (50% of total tuition)
benefits: 50% Tuition waiver (USD 30,972 of the USD 61,944 published total tuition)
Scholarship benefits are subject to the academic performance of the scholarship recipient and based on the availability of funds
Open to new applicants as well as current AUWCL students from an OAS member state (except the United States) who are not current OAS scholarship recipients
eligibility: Be admitted to one of the LL.M. programs offered by American University Washington College of Law
Be a citizen and/or permanent legal resident of any active OAS member state, except the United States
Hold a Juris Doctor (JD) from a US law school accredited by the American Bar Association (ABA), or a first degree in law from a foreign law school with equivalent standards
Not be a current OAS scholarship recipient
Not be a citizen and/or permanent resident of the United States, nor GS/OAS staff or their immediate relatives or GS/OAS consultants, nor OAS Permanent officials or their immediate relatives
Applicants from Argentina must fill out the required form and send it to the National Liaison Office (ONE) in Argentina
requirements: Submit a completed application through AUWCL's website along with supporting documents before the application deadline
Provide all documentation requested by AUWCL; once admitted, AUWCL will issue an Admissions Letter to be considered for the scholarship
Sign an OAS/AUWCL Acceptance Form accepting the scholarship and agreeing to its terms and conditions
Maintain satisfactory academic performance with a GPA of at least 3.0/4.0 to retain the scholarship
Commit to return to work in the sponsoring country or permanent legal residence in an OAS member state, or at an international organization, for at least the duration of the scholarship
documents: Completed AUWCL online application form submitted through AUWCL's website
All supporting documentation requested by AUWCL for admission
Admissions Letter issued by AUWCL once admitted
English Language Proficiency documentation for international applicants in the English-language programs
Signed OAS/AUWCL Acceptance Form (awarded candidates only)
selection_criteria: The merits and overall credentials of the candidate, including academic and professional background
Geographical distribution of the applicants, taking into account the greater needs of the smaller and relatively less developed economies
Applicants whose essays portray the highest potential for impact upon return to their countries of origin
coverage: 50% of the LL.M. tuition fee (USD 30,972 of the USD 61,944 published total tuition)
2026-2027 academic credit price is USD 2,581, expected to increase 3-5% each academic year
application_method: Apply for admission to the AUWCL LL.M. programme online at https://www.american.edu/wcl/academics/degrees/llm/how-to-apply/online.cfm with the supporting documents AUWCL requires, before the application deadline
International applicants must meet AUWCL's English Language Proficiency Requirement (English programs only); the Spanish-language programme does not require English proficiency
Once admitted into the program, AUWCL issues an Admissions Letter, which is the document considered for the scholarship
Selected awardees are contacted by the OAS by email with the scholarship offer and acceptance instructions, and sign the OAS/AUWCL Acceptance Form
Applicants from Argentina must fill out the required DGCIN form and send it to the National Liaison Office (ONE) in Argentina
official.application_route: Apply for admission through AUWCL's online application; scholarship consideration follows from the AUWCL Admissions Letter, and awardees sign the OAS/AUWCL Acceptance Form.
official.study_mode: Onsite (English programs only), hybrid or online
official.citizenship_residency: Citizens and/or permanent legal residents of any active OAS member state, except the United States.
official.international_eligibility: Open to international applicants - citizens and/or permanent legal residents of OAS member states other than the United States; open to new applicants as well as current AUWCL students.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Limited to the LL.M. programs offered by AUWCL: LL.M. in International Human Rights and Humanitarian Law, LL.M. en Derechos Humanos y Derecho Humanitario, and LL.M. in International Arbitration and Business Law.
official.duration: LL.M. in International Human Rights and Humanitarian Law: 2-3 semesters; LL.M. en Derechos Humanos y Derecho Humanitario: 2-10 semesters; LL.M. in International Arbitration and Business Law: 9-18 months.
official.description: Under the OAS Partnerships Program for Education and Training (PAEC), the OAS-AUWCL Scholarship Program awards a 50% tuition waiver for the LL.M. programs of American University Washington College of Law in Washington, D.C., offered onsite, hybrid or online.
official.region: Washington, D.C., United States (onsite, hybrid or online)
official.program_type: Regional intergovernmental scholarship programme - OAS Partnerships Program for Education and Training (PAEC) with American University Washington College of Law
official.english_requirement: International applicants must meet AUWCL's English Language Proficiency Requirement (English programs only); the Spanish-language programme does not require English proficiency.

Number of scholarships awarded is not stated
The exact list of AUWCL admission documents is not enumerated - the announcement requires 'all documentation requested by AUWCL'
verification.notes: The 50% tuition waiver, the USD 61,944 total tuition and USD 30,972 scholar balance, programme durations and modalities, Spring 2027 deadlines, eligibility and ineligibility rules, selection criteria, uncovered expenses and recipient duties were verified in the official OAS PAEC announcement PDF on oas.org, cross-checked against the OAS Scholarships open-announcements page, on 2026-10-10.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a 50% tuition waiver worth USD 30,972 against the published USD 61,944 total tuition for the AUWCL LL.M. programs, open only to citizens and/or permanent legal residents of OAS member states other than the United States. You must first win admission through AUWCL, because the Admissions Letter the school issues on admission is what puts you into scholarship consideration. Spring 2027 deadlines are 1 November 2026 for the residential track and 30 November 2026 for hybrid and online tracks, with classes beginning January 2027. Recipients must keep a 3.0/4.0 GPA and commit to returning to their home country for at least the length of the scholarship, and every other cost - fees, insurance, books, visa, travel and living expenses - stays with you.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Law graduates from OAS member states outside the U.S. who can fund the remaining half of tuition plus Washington, D.C. living costs and want a U.S. LL.M. in human rights, humanitarian law or international arbitration.
application_readiness_checklist: Start the AUWCL admission application early enough that you are admitted before the modality-specific scholarship deadline (1 November 2026 residential; 30 November 2026 hybrid/online)
Prepare English proficiency evidence if applying to an English-language track; the Spanish LL.M. does not require it
Budget the remaining 50% of tuition plus mandatory fees, health insurance, books, visa and graduation costs, and D.C. living expenses before committing
Explore the OAS Rowe Fund (interest-free loans up to USD 15,000) as a separate funding route for the balance
Argentine applicants: complete the DGCIN form and send it to the National Liaison Office (ONE) in Argentina
Draft the essay around concrete impact you will have on return to your country of origin, since that is an explicit selection criterion
common_rejection_risks: Applying for the scholarship without first securing AUWCL admission - consideration only begins once AUWCL issues the Admissions Letter
Holding a current OAS scholarship, being a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, or being GS/OAS staff, a GS/OAS consultant, an OAS Permanent official or their immediate relative
Assuming the waiver covers more than 50% of tuition - fees, insurance, books, travel, visa and living costs are the recipient's sole responsibility
An essay that does not demonstrate clear potential for impact upon return to the country of origin
Missing the modality-specific deadline - residential and hybrid/online tracks have different dates
Underestimating future tuition increases on longer tracks such as the 2-10 semester Spanish-language program
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The remaining 50% of tuition (USD 30,972 at 2026-27 prices), mandatory university fees, books and study materials, health insurance, graduation expenses, visa expenses, travel to and from the country of study, and all other living and study costs in Washington, D.C.
document_audit: The Admissions Letter comes only after admission, so admission timing effectively gates the scholarship application
English proficiency documentation is required only for the English-language programmes
Everything else is whatever AUWCL requests for admission - the announcement does not publish a fixed document list, so track the admissions office requirements directly
Winning candidates must sign the OAS/AUWCL Acceptance Form before the award is formally granted
Argentine applicants have an extra national paperwork step through the ONE in Argentina
alerts: The 2026-2027 academic credit price of USD 2,581 is expected to increase 3-5% each academic year, so the balance you pay grows over multi-semester tracks
Declining the scholarship after the program start date without proof of force majeure can trigger reimbursement of all funding granted
Recipients must commit to return to their sponsoring country (or an international organization) for at least the duration of the scholarship; failure can trigger reimbursement of the total value
Selection results are published only in August and December, and applicants who are not selected will not be contacted
The General Secretariat reserves the right to cancel the scholarship announcement at any time during the process
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the AUWCL admission application online with all requested documents; on admission AUWCL issues the Admissions Letter that enters you into scholarship consideration; the OAS emails selected candidates the offer and the OAS/AUWCL Acceptance Form formalizes the award.
